name: SERS spectra of nine bacterial strains (E. coli, P. aeruginosa, S. aureus) on an anisotropic gold nanorod array (Gulmus et al. 2026)
description: 117 SERS spectra of nine bacterial strains (3 each of E. coli 29922/K4/BAA-2523, P. aeruginosa 9027/10145/27853 and S. aureus 6538/25923/43300) on an anisotropic gold nanorod array (Gulmus et al. 2026; the associated article is under review, so the Zenodo record v1.0.1, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23426967, is the citation; the repo's earlier v1.0.0 record is doi:10.5281/zenodo.23284998). WITec alpha 300R confocal Raman microscope, 785 nm excitation, x50 objective, 10 mW, ~3.03 s integration, 4 cm^-1 spectral resolution. Each strain was cultivated once and deposited as one 5 uL (0.5 McFarland) droplet on a single GNA substrate; all 13 spectra of a strain were recorded from that droplet on the same day, so group_ids = strain (9 groups of 13) and leave-strain-out is the paper's validation protocol (it also analyses acquisition-order trends within each strain). The loader reads the raw WITec instrument text files (counts, before any baseline correction, smoothing or normalization): all 117 share one 1,024-point 247.99-1,997.9 cm^-1 axis (non-uniform, 1.44-2.04 cm^-1 spacing), used as is. The deposit's preprocessed CSV (Data S1; OPUS 5.5 rubberband + Savitzky-Golay + min-max normalization, 1,215 points, with the S. aureus spectra exported on a 0-1 scale and the other two species on 0-2) is not loaded. Labels are the three species (39 spectra each) and groups the nine strains, so grouped CV predicts the species of a strain the model has not seen. Strain identity is not exposed as a label: each strain is a single droplet, so strain labels with strain groups would leave every test class unseen, and without groups a strain classifier could learn the droplet instead of the strain. The repo is served as a commit-pinned archive (1028526, size + sha256 pinned; the Zenodo v1.0.1 archive's data are byte-identical).

rai:dataCollection: SERS measurements (WITec alpha 300R, 785 nm, x50, 10 mW, ~3.03 s) of 9 x 13 spectra from single-droplet deposits of nine bacterial strains on one anisotropic gold nanorod array substrate, 250-2,000 cm^-1 region, 1,024 points per spectrum.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: None in the loader: raw WITec instrument counts as exported (no baseline correction, smoothing or normalization; no wavelength or position correction recorded in the deposit).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each spectrum is labelled with the species of its droplet (E. coli, P. aeruginosa, S. aureus; 39 spectra each) and grouped by strain (three per species), assigned from the known cultivation/deposit order. No human labelling of spectra was involved.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is included. All spectra originate from cultured bacterial samples without individual human identifiers.
rai:dataBiases: Single lab, single instrument, single substrate type and single acquisition day: all 13 spectra of a strain come from one droplet of one culture (strong within-strain correlation; group_ids = strain, 9 groups). The strains were acquired in a fixed species-interleaved sequence, so acquisition order is confounded with strain and the paper analyses the resulting order trends (drift); a model may learn drift artifacts instead of biology. SERS intensity is substrate-position dependent, so absolute intensities are not comparable across spots or substrates. Nine classes of 13 spectra each is a small set; results may not generalise to other strains, species or SERS substrates.
rai:dataLimitations: The loader ships the raw instrument files (counts before baseline correction, smoothing or normalization). The deposit's preprocessed CSV (Data S1: OPUS rubberband + Savitzky-Golay + min-max, 1,215 points, with S. aureus exported on a 0-1 scale and the other species on 0-2) is not loaded. Only nine strains (three per species) are covered, one droplet/substrate per strain; within-strain replicates share one physical sample, so leave-strain-out is the protocol-honest split (9 groups). The associated article is under review (no article DOI yet); citation is via the Zenodo record (v1.0.1, 2026-10-17).
rai:dataSocialImpact: Supports research into rapid, label-free identification of bacterial strains by SERS (e.g. antimicrobial-resistance screening workflows); any diagnostic use requires validation across strains, labs and substrates by qualified microbiologists.
rai:dataUseCases: 3-class species classification from single-spot SERS spectra of unseen strains; group-aware CV is leave-strain-out (9 groups of 13). Strain is not a label (each strain is a single droplet, so strain identity cannot be separated from the droplet); analysis of acquisition-order drift is supported by the manifest's acquisition_order column in the deposit.
